column1: # Lines of bom_combination_matrix.tsv that rledger counts further from
# beancount 3.2.3 than main does, each accepted by hand. Kept by hand:
# `BOM_MATRIX_UPDATE` never writes this file, and tests/bom_combination_matrix.rs
# fails on any further-than-main line not listed here, or listed with
# another cause than the rules give. One per line:
#   <source after the two `open` lines>  <line>  <cause>  <alone>  <why>
# <alone> is beancount's count for the line alone after the head (under a
# bare `2024-01-02 *` header when indented), and must agree with the table's
# own column; `-` where the cause is checked another way. How each cause is
# checked:
# - a recovery cause (the line is wrong only after the lines before it):
#   rledger counts the line alone as beancount does alone;
# - `like-main-without-bom`: the analog columns (the input with its BOMs
#   replaced by ordinary characters) are beancount's and rledger's counts;
# - `inner-bom-under-line-error`: the line has BOMs inside beancount's own
#   invalid tokens (by beancount's lexer, so not inside an account, which
#   admits a BOM), and with each made a `$` rledger counts the line as
#   beancount does;
# - `bom-account-under-line-diagnostic`: a BOM-led account (by beancount's
#   lexer) starts on the line, and with each written `Assets:X` rledger
#   counts the line as beancount does;
# - `one-diagnostic-per-line`: rledger counts beancount's count less
#   exactly beancount's grammar errors after the line's first error (a table
#   column), its one diagnostic standing for that first error;
# - `invalid-account-after-invalid-token`: alone, rledger is off the same
#   way and at least as far as in context (or counts the line the same
#   alone, where beancount reports less in context after the line before);
# - `bom-glued-to-account`, `mid-line-hash-bang`, and a composite of parts
#   joined by `&` (`bom-glued-to-account&mid-line-hash-bang`,
#   `bom-glued-to-account&extra-construct-error`): each part is taken out
#   in turn and its share measured (the glued BOMs: the errors that go when
#   each account beancount reads with its BOMs is written `Assets:X`, no
#   more than the line's `P0026`s; the `#!` / `#+`: what goes with each made
#   an ordinary invalid run, against beancount's count for that input; the
#   construct error: main's overcount of the BOM-free analog), each share is
#   not zero, and together they are exactly the line's difference. The glued
#   and construct shares are positive; the `#!` / `#+` share is that of a
#   lone capital glued to it (`T#!`), one invalid token in beancount
#   (#2928 made a mid-line `#!` / `#+` a `#` and the token after it).
